simple: the place in a program where the lanes that split at an if or a loop wait for each other and go on together.
analogy: the spot where a row of helpers lines up again before its next step.
precise: a program point after a divergent branch at which the hardware resumes executing the warp or wavefront with the combined mask; in this build's SASS it is set by SSY (sm_60) or BSSY (sm_80) and reached at SYNC or BSYNC.
source: R9 and R11 of BR-03 (compiler output, CUDA 12.0); D1 and D11 of BR-03 (NVIDIA "CUDA C++ Programming Guide", "CUDA Binary Utilities") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
related: SIMT deadlock (spin lock in a warp)

simple: newer NVIDIA GPUs can let the lanes of one warp make progress on different paths in turn.
analogy: helpers of a row may take separate small steps, although the row still prefers to move together.
precise: NVIDIA's execution model since the Volta generation (compute capability 7.0), in which each thread keeps its own program counter and call stack, so divergent paths of a warp may interleave; warp intrinsics therefore take an explicit participation mask (_sync suffix).
source: D1 of BR-03 (NVIDIA "CUDA C++ Programming Guide", SIMT architecture; compute capability 7.x) — written from memory, pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a promise that a waiting thread will eventually let the thread it waits for run.
analogy: sooner or later the cook with the key gets a turn at the stove.
precise: a property of a scheduler or execution model stating which threads are guaranteed to keep executing while others wait; a lock is safe only if the lock holder is guaranteed to progress while waiters spin.
source: D1 and D7 of BR-03 (NVIDIA "CUDA C++ Programming Guide"; McKenney, "Is Parallel Programming Hard, And, If So, What Can You Do About It?") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
related: SIMT deadlock (spin lock in a warp)

term: SIMT deadlock (spin lock in a warp)
simple: a warp hangs because the lane holding a lock waits for its own warp, and the rest of the warp waits for the lock.
analogy: the helper with the key waits for her row; the row waits for the key.
precise: a deadlock between lanes of one group under lock-step execution: the lock owner has left the spin loop and waits at the reconvergence point, which lies before the unlock, while the other lanes keep spinning; avoided by doing the work and the unlock inside the loop, or by not locking at all (atomics, privatization).
source: R9 and R10 of BR-03 (SASS of the spin lock, CUDA 12.0; the chapter's lock-step model); whether a given GPU hangs: D1 of BR-03, pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: two ways to share a long list among workers: each takes one solid block, or each takes every T-th item.
analogy: each cook takes a quarter of the sack, versus helpers side by side taking neighbouring beans.
precise: chunked: worker t of T processes indices [n·t/T, n·(t+1)/T); interleaved: t, t + T, t + 2T, …. On a GPU the interleaved form lets the lanes of a group touch neighbouring addresses in one instruction (coalescing); on a CPU the chunked form gives each core one contiguous stream.
source: R2 and R12 of BR-03 (CPU measurement and the chapter's access-pattern model); D2 of BR-03 (NVIDIA "CUDA C++ Best Practices Guide", coalesced access) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
